architecture_alternatives.candidate_ceiling: Recall cannot exceed the frozen BM25 top-50 candidate recall for each query.
confounds: Prompt-RAG quality includes dependence on BM25 candidate coverage.
architecture_alternatives.label: BM25 top-50 plus LLM relevance reranking
architecture_alternatives.structural_rationale: Smallest auditable staged design consistent with the documentation-only reranking description; deterministic first stage and explicit ceiling.

architecture_alternatives.candidate_ceiling: Recall cannot exceed the frozen Phase 4 Hybrid top-50 candidate recall for each query.
confounds: The reported Prompt-RAG system would inherit both Hybrid components.
A Prompt-RAG comparison against Hybrid would not isolate the reranker's contribution.
architecture_alternatives.label: Hybrid top-50 plus LLM relevance reranking

architecture_alternatives.candidate_ceiling: All 140 chunks are candidates, so there is no first-stage candidate-recall ceiling.
confounds: This is direct corpus scoring rather than the documented reranking design.
It substantially increases context, calls, tokens, cost, and ordering sensitivity.
architecture_alternatives.label: Direct all-corpus LLM relevance scoring

architecture_alternatives.candidate_ceiling: Depends on an undefined downstream retriever and depth.
confounds: Introduces a second LLM behavior and additional failure modes.
No reachable repository evidence defines rewriting behavior.
Creates broad prompt-tuning degrees of freedom.
architecture_alternatives.label: LLM query rewriting followed by retrieval or reranking

candidate_recall_ceiling_reporting.calculation_time: only after the trace gate and authorized ranking run, alongside exploratory metrics
candidate_recall_ceiling_reporting.definition: For each query, the fraction of frozen judged-gold evidence present in the first-stage candidate set; report per query and aggregate without treating unjudged chunks as nonrelevant facts.

fair_comparison_controls: Use exactly the frozen 140-chunk corpus and 34 R5 questions.
Keep chunk IDs as retrieval units.
Do not read qrels, reference answers, categories, sealed provenance, owner judgments, or metrics when constructing model inputs or prompts.
Do not train or tune against the benchmark.
Do not use BM25, FAISS, Graph, or Hybrid performance results to optimize the prompt or architecture.
Do not add manual query-specific rules.
Do not expose hidden gold evidence to any system.
Name a staged system as a reranker and identify its first-stage generator and depth.
Preserve missing and invalid responses as failures.
Do not substitute BM25 or another retriever for failures.
Freeze all execution parameters before any authorized run.

risk_register.control: Freeze generator/depth and report candidate recall ceiling.
risk_register.risk: First-stage ceiling may be misattributed to the LLM reranker.

risk_register.control: Strict allowlisted fields and tests; no gold-related paths in runtime config.
risk_register.risk: Gold, category, answer, provenance, or prior-result leakage into prompt design or model input.

risk_register.control: Owner selects architecture for structural reasons before results; config remains execution-disabled.
risk_register.risk: Architecture choice based on likely or observed benchmark gain.

risk_register.control: Pin provider/model/version/SDK and preserve exact request/response traces.
Fixed ordering, explicit batching, repeated trace audit, deterministic parser and tie rule.
risk_register.risk: Candidate order or stochastic output changes ranking.

risk_register.control: Fail closed and count errors/retries; no hidden fallback or backfill.
risk_register.risk: API failures are silently replaced, biasing retrieval quality upward.

risk_register.control: Separate Phase 5A retrieval protocol from the later H5 answer-generation protocol.
risk_register.risk: Retrieval and generation effects are conflated.
